Issue 18, by the Trail Notes editors

Every experienced hiker has a story about a bluebird morning that turned. The lesson is rarely that the forecast was wrong, it is that the signs on the hill were ignored.

Those smooth lens-shaped caps over the summit mean strong winds aloft. They look calm and they are anything but, plan for gusts on exposed ridgelines.

If the cap thickens or drops within two hours of first spotting it, shorten the route. Weather that builds fast tends to arrive faster.

Now I'll review the defects and fix them.

**Defect found:** The heading structure is non-semantic and skips levels — the page title is marked `<h3>`, followed by `<h5>`, `<h6>`, `<h5>`, with no `<h1>` at all. This breaks WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 2.4.6 (Headings and Labels): screen reader users navigating by heading level get a confusing, non-hierarchical outline and no page-title heading. I'll fix the underlying markup (not just visuals) by renumbering to `h1 > h2 > h3 > h2`, and update the CSS selectors so the visual design is unchanged.

The button (`Subscribe free`) is already a real native `<button>` with `data-track`, so it's keyboard-operable and fires the instrumentation script correctly via click — no change needed there. No images, adequate contrast on body/byline text (~5.17:1), no ARIA retrofits or focus traps present.

content.text:
## Summary

**Defect found:** The document had a broken/non-semantic heading structure — the article title was marked as `<h3 class="title">`, and body headings used `<h5>` and `<h6>`, with no `<h1>` anywhere and heading levels skipping around (h3 → h5 → h6 → h5). This fails WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) and 2.4.6 (Headings and Labels): screen reader/keyboard users who navigate by heading level get a confusing, out-of-order outline and no proper page title heading to orient by.

**Fix:** Renumbered the headings to a correct, sequential hierarchy while keeping every visible word, class, and layout identical:
- `<h3 class="title">` → `<h1 class="title">` (the page's single title heading)
- Both `<h5>` section headings → `<h2>`
- `<h6>` sub-heading → `<h3>`
- Updated the corresponding CSS selectors (`h3.title`, `h5`, `h6` → `h1.title`, `h2`, `h3`) so font sizes/margins are pixel-identical to before — purely a tag rename, zero visual change.

**Left alone (already compliant):**
- The `Subscribe free` control is already a native `<button type="button">` with `data-track="subscribe"` — it's natively keyboard-focusable and activatable (Enter/Space), and native activation fires a real `click` event, so the instrumentation script's delegated listener records `window.__activated` correctly for both mouse and keyboard. No ARIA retrofit or JS handler was needed or added.
- `<header>` and `<main>` landmarks, `lang="en"`, and viewport meta were already correct.
- Text contrast (byline ~5.17:1, body text, button text) already meets AA; no color changes made.
- No images, no custom widgets, no focus-trap risks, and no outline-suppressing CSS were present, so nothing needed touching there.

The instrumentation script, all `id`/`data-track` attributes, visible text, and visual design are unchanged — the diff is limited to the heading tag names and their matching CSS selectors.

status_detail: heading hierarchy fixed (h3→h1, h5→h2, h6→h3); CSS updated; visual zero-change
